docs.title: Find the page you saved, even when you forget its name
docs.text:
MemoryLane is a personal memory for the web. You save pages as you browse, with one click or automatically, and later find them by describing what they were about. You don't need the exact title, URL or wording.

Open MemoryLane → · Get the extension →

Browse → Save → Clean → Chunk → Embed → Store
                                          ↓
      Find ← Rank ← Fuse ← Keyword + meaning search ← Describe it

docs.title: What MemoryLane can do
docs.text:
• One-click saving from the Chrome extension, with undo
  • Automatic capture (off by default) that skips sensitive and low-value pages and any site you exclude
  • Search by meaning or by exact words: hybrid BM25 + vector search, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
  • Readable snippets that show the sentences matching your query
  • Library map: your saved pages grouped into named topics on a zoomable map
  • Related pages for any saved page
  • Search within a topic from the map
  • On-demand summaries of a single result (Gemini)
  • YouTube videos, saved through their transcripts
  • Voice search in browsers that support speech recognition
  • Private accounts: sign in with Google or email; every page belongs to one account only
  • Export or delete all your data at any time

docs.title: Why MemoryLane?
docs.text:
Browser history tells you where you went. MemoryLane helps you remember what was there.

Instead of an exact page or phrase, you can search for something like:

"that article explaining how database query latency can be reduced"

MemoryLane searches the text of the pages you saved and returns the pages that match best, with the most relevant sentences shown.

docs.title: Main components
docs.text:
Component Role Chrome extension (Manifest V3) Saves the current page, auto-capture, excluded sites Svelte web app Search, library, map, related pages, summaries, account Amazon Cognito Sign-in (Google or email) for the web app and the extension Caddy HTTPS, serves the web app, proxies /api to the backend FastAPI backend Verifies tokens, saves pages, searches, builds the map trafilatura Extracts the readable text of a page Sentence Transformers (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) 384-dimensional embeddings Apache Solr 9.7 Stores chunks; BM25 and vector (KNN) search scikit-learn Topic clustering for the library map Gemini Optional: result summaries and map topic names

Everything runs with Docker Compose on a single AWS EC2 instance, served at memorylane.site.

docs.title: Browser extension
docs.text:
The Chrome extension saves the current page with Remember this page, and lets you undo a save straight away. Automatic capture is optional and off by default, and you can exclude any site from it. Alt+Shift+M opens the MemoryLane website.

More on saving pages

docs.title: Content extraction
docs.text: Each saved page is cleaned with trafilatura, so menus, footers, cookie banners and adverts stay out of your library. YouTube videos are saved through their transcripts.

docs.title: Hybrid search
docs.text:
Search runs keyword (BM25) and meaning (vector) retrieval together and combines them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Each result shows a short snippet of the sentences that best match the query.

Example:

"Find documentation about ROS navigation"

More on search

docs.title: Library and library map
docs.text:
The library lists every saved page, newest first, and you can delete pages with undo. The map groups your pages into named topics. From the map you can open a page, see its related pages, or search within one topic.

More on the library · More on the map

docs.title: Summaries
docs.text: Each search result has a Summarise button that asks Gemini for a short summary of that page.

docs.title: Accounts and privacy
docs.text:
You sign in with Google or with email (Amazon Cognito). Every page belongs to one account, and every search, summary and listing sees only your own pages. You can export or delete all your data from the account menu.

More on privacy

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: MemoryLane holds personal browsing information, so privacy is part of the design rather than an add-on.

docs.title: Accounts and isolation
docs.text:
• You sign in with Google or with email through Amazon Cognito. MemoryLane never sees your password.
  • The backend takes your user id from the verified access token (its sub claim). No endpoint accepts a user id from the browser.
  • Every read, write, search, summary, map and delete in Solr is filtered by that user id. A page id is derived from your user id and the URL, so two people saving the same page get separate copies.
  • Asking for another person's page returns 404, the same as a page that doesn't exist.

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text:
For each page you save: its URL, title, cleaned text, a short description, the time you saved it, and the embeddings used for search and for the map.

The data lives in Solr on the MemoryLane server (AWS, Mumbai region). Solr is bound to the server's localhost and is not reachable from the internet; only Caddy (HTTPS) is public.

docs.title: Automatic capture
docs.text:
Automatic capture is off by default. It only runs when you're signed in and have turned it on in the extension. Even then, the extension skips:

  • Social-media sites
  • Banks and payment services
  • Login, sign-up, account, password, checkout, billing, payment and wallet pages
  • Browser-internal pages (chrome://, extensions, file://, ...)
  • Search-engine result pages
  • Utility pages such as error, privacy, terms, cookie and sitemap pages
  • Files such as PDFs, images, media, archives, CSV, JSON and XML
  • Any site you add to Excluded sites in the extension
  • MemoryLane's own website

The filtering happens in the extension, before anything is sent.

docs.title: What is sent to Google Gemini
docs.text:
Gemini is optional. When the server has a Gemini key:

  • Summaries: the text of one page is sent when you press Summarise on that result.
  • Map topic names: when your map is built, the titles of a sample of pages in each topic (and a few keywords) are sent once so the topics get readable names. Names are cached, so this only happens again when a topic's pages change.

Without a key, summaries are turned off and the map names topics from their keywords instead. Nothing else leaves the server.

docs.title: Export or delete
docs.text:
From the account menu (top right of the website):

  • Export my data downloads every page you saved as JSON.
  • Delete all my data removes all your pages from the index.

Single pages can be deleted from the library, search results or the map, with a few seconds to undo.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
People read a lot online but struggle to find it again later.

Students, developers, researchers and professionals often read useful resources but forget:

  • Website names
  • URLs
  • Exact keywords
  • Where the information was found

docs.title: Browser history
docs.text: Browser history only matches titles and URLs, so you need to remember the website name or a word from the title.

docs.title: Bookmarks
docs.text: Bookmarks have to be saved and organised by hand, and are searched by title only.

docs.title: Search engines
docs.text: Search engines search the whole internet, not the pages you personally read.

docs.title: Proposed solution
docs.text:
MemoryLane is a personal memory layer over the pages you read. It stores their text, and you search it by describing what you remember instead of typing exact keywords.

Example:

"Find that article about reinforcement learning I read last week"

MemoryLane returns the page with a snippet of the matching sentences. From there you can see related pages and the topic the page belongs to on your library map.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: The MemoryLane API is a FastAPI application. On the live site it is served under https://memorylane.site/api. Locally it runs at http://localhost:8000 with no /api prefix.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every endpoint except GET /health needs a Cognito access token:

Authorization: Bearer <access token>

Missing, expired or invalid tokens get 401. The user is always the token's subject, so no endpoint takes a user id. See Security.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Purpose GET /health Public status of Solr, the embedding model and Gemini POST /memory Save (or update) a page GET /memory/status Is this URL saved? DELETE /memory/{page_id} Delete a page GET /memory/{page_id}/related Pages closest in meaning to this one GET /memories Saved pages, newest first POST /search Hybrid search, optionally within a map topic POST /summarize Gemini summary of one page GET /map The library map GET /map/search Find topics and pages on the map GET /me/export Download all your pages as JSON DELETE /me/data Delete all your pages

Request and response models are in backend/models.py. FastAPI's interactive docs are at /docs when running locally.

See Endpoints for details.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Status Meaning 400 Missing required input (e.g. empty query) 401 No valid access token 404 Page not found, or not yours 409 Topic search on a map that has since changed 422 Invalid input, or a page with fewer than 50 words 429 Rate limit exceeded 502 / 503 Gemini failed / is not configured (summaries only)

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text: Paths are relative to the API base (https://memorylane.site/api on the live site). All endpoints except /health need a bearer token. The rate limit is per user.

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Public. Reports whether the backend's dependencies are ready.

{ "status": "ok", "solr": true, "embedding_model": true, "gemini": true }

status is ok when Solr and the embedding model are ready. gemini: false only means summaries are off.

docs.title: POST /memory
docs.text:
Save a page, or update it if it's already saved. Rate limit: 60/minute.

{
  "url": "https://example.com/article",
  "title": "Example Article",
  "content": "Visible text of the page...",
  "html": "<!doctype html>...",
  "canonical_url": "https://example.com/article",
  "is_manual": true
}

html and canonical_url are optional. When html is present, the main text is extracted from it; content is the fallback.

{
  "status": "saved",
  "message": "Memory stored successfully",
  "page": {
    "id": "3f9c...", "url": "https://example.com/article", "title": "Example Article",
    "domain": "example.com", "timestamp": "2026-10-22T09:30:00Z", "chunks": 4
  }
}

status is saved, unchanged (same text as before) or skipped (e.g. a YouTube video that can't be saved). A page with fewer than 50 words gets 422.

docs.title: GET /memory/status?url=...&canonical_url=...
docs.text:
Whether you've saved this URL, normalised the same way as a save. Rate limit: 120/minute.

{ "saved": true, "page": { "id": "3f9c...", "url": "...", "title": "...", "domain": "...", "timestamp": "..." } }

docs.title: DELETE /memory/{page_id}
docs.text: Delete one of your pages. Returns 204, or 404 if it isn't yours. Rate limit: 60/minute.

docs.title: GET /memory/{page_id}/related?k=5
docs.text:
Your other pages closest in meaning to this one (k from 1 to 20). Rate limit: 120/minute.

{
  "page_id": "3f9c...",
  "related": [
    { "id": "a1b2...", "title": "...", "url": "...", "domain": "...", "saved_at": "...", "similarity": 0.81 }
  ]
}

docs.title: GET /memories?limit=20&offset=0
docs.text:
Your pages, newest first (limit up to 100). Rate limit: 60/minute.

{ "total": 278, "pages": [ { "id": "...", "url": "...", "title": "...", "domain": "...", "timestamp": "...", "chunks": 3 } ] }

docs.title: POST /search
docs.text:
Hybrid search over your pages. Rate limit: 60/minute.

{
  "query": "documentation about ROS navigation",
  "num_results": 10,
  "summarize": false,
  "debug": false,
  "topic": null
}
Field Notes query Required, up to 500 characters num_results 1–20, default 10 summarize Also summarise each result with Gemini (slow; the web app uses /summarize per result instead) debug Add ranks, scores and timings topic A topic id from GET /map: search only that topic's pages. 409 if the map has changed 
{
  "query": "documentation about ROS navigation",
  "results": [
    {
      "rank": 1, "id": "3f9c...", "title": "Nav2 Documentation", "url": "...",
      "domain": "docs.nav2.org", "timestamp": "...",
      "snippet": "Nav2 is the professionally supported successor of the ROS Navigation Stack...",
      "summary": null
    }
  ]
}

With debug: true, each result also has bm25_rank, knn_rank, fused_score, rerank_score and vector_similarity, and the response has timings in milliseconds.

docs.title: POST /summarize
docs.text:
Summarise one of your pages with Gemini. Rate limit: 20/minute.

{ "query": "brief overview", "id": "3f9c..." }

{ "id": "3f9c...", "summary": "..." }

404 if the page isn't yours, 503 if Gemini isn't configured, 502 if it failed.

docs.title: GET /map
docs.text:
Your library map. Rate limit: 30/minute.

{
  "status": "ok",
  "version": "9b1e4c",
  "topics": [ { "id": "9b1e4c-3", "label": "Protein Folding", "count": 31, "x": 0.42, "y": 0.38, "rx": 0.09, "ry": 0.065 } ],
  "pages": [ { "id": "3f9c...", "title": "...", "url": "...", "domain": "...", "saved_at": "...", "x": 0.44, "y": 0.36, "topic": "9b1e4c-3" } ],
  "edges": [ { "a": "3f9c...", "b": "a1b2...", "kind": "intra" } ],
  "topic_links": [ { "a": "9b1e4c-3", "b": "9b1e4c-7" } ],
  "counts": { "pages": 278, "topics": 9, "unclustered": 12, "without_vectors": 0 }
}

Coordinates are in a 0–1 box. A page with topic: null is unclustered. With fewer than 10 pages the response is { "status": "too_few", "count": 6, ... }.

docs.title: GET /map/search?q=...
docs.text:
Find topics on your map by name and by the pages inside them. Rate limit: 120/minute.

{ "query": "proteins", "version": "9b1e4c", "topics": [ { "id": "9b1e4c-3", "label": "Protein Folding", "score": 0.74 } ], "pages": ["3f9c...", "..."] }

docs.title: GET /me/export
docs.text: Downloads memorylane-export.json with every page you saved (URL, title, timestamp and full text), newest first. Rate limit: 5/minute.

docs.title: DELETE /me/data
docs.text: Deletes all your pages. Returns 204. Rate limit: 5/minute.

docs.title: Backend Architecture
docs.text: The backend is a FastAPI application in code/src/backend.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
backend/
├── main.py           API endpoints, rate limits, CORS, error handling
├── auth.py           Cognito access-token verification → user_id
├── models.py         Pydantic request and response models
├── config.py         Settings from .env
├── ingest.py         ingest_page: the one way a page gets saved
├── cleaning.py       trafilatura extraction, junk-line removal, descriptions
├── url_utils.py      URL normalisation and page ids
├── youtube_utils.py  Video ids, metadata and transcripts
├── chunking.py       Sentence-aware overlapping chunks
├── embeddings.py     Sentence Transformers model, passage and query embeddings
├── retrieval.py      Hybrid search: BM25 + KNN, RRF, grouping, relevance floor
├── rerank.py         Optional cross-encoder reranker
├── snippets.py       Query-focused snippets
├── library_map.py    Topics, labels, layout, links, per-user map cache
├── summarizer.py     Gemini summaries and topic names
├── solr_client.py    Every Solr call, always scoped by user_id
├── page_filter.py    Server copy of the URL eligibility rules
└── cli.py            Command-line search

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
1. Rate limiting (slowapi): per user once authenticated, otherwise per IP. Limits range from 5/minute (export, delete all) to 120/minute (status checks, related pages, map search).
  2. Authentication: the current_user_id dependency verifies the bearer token and returns its sub. Every endpoint except /health requires it.
  3. The endpoint calls ingest_page, hybrid_search, map_service or the summariser with that user id.
  4. Solr calls go through SolrClient, which adds the user_id filter to every query and rejects malformed ids.

docs.title: Start-up
docs.text: The embedding model loads at start-up so the first save or search is fast. The API refuses to start if the Cognito settings are missing.

docs.title: Caches
docs.text: Cache Scope Cleared when Query embeddings last 1,024 queries process restart Sentence embeddings for snippets LRU of 4,096 sentences process restart Library map per user, 50 users, 10-minute TTL the user saves or deletes a page Topic labels per topic membership process restart

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: Script Purpose scripts/setup_solr.sh / .ps1 Create the core and install the schema, with a smoke test scripts/add_description_field.sh Add the description field to an existing core scripts/add_page_embedding_field.sh Add the page_embedding field to an existing core scripts/backfill_page_vectors.py Give older pages a page vector (resumable) scripts/reindex.py Copy pages from another core under a user id

docs.title: Web app
docs.text:
The web app is built with Svelte 4 and Vite, in code/src/frontend. It has no UI framework: colours, type (IBM Plex Sans and Mono) and spacing come from design tokens in styles/tokens.css, in a monochrome dark theme.

frontend/src/
├── App.svelte            Routing: signed-out landing vs. the app
├── auth.js               Cognito PKCE sign-in, token refresh, sign-out
├── api.js                Authenticated fetch; 401 → refresh once → retry
├── stores.ts             Shared state (recent pages, query, ...)
├── mapStore.js           Loads and caches the library map
├── pageDeletes.js        Delete-with-undo queue
├── routes/
│   ├── Landing.svelte    Signed-out home
│   ├── Home.svelte       Search box + recently saved
│   ├── Results.svelte    Results, snippets, summaries, topic filter
│   ├── Library.svelte    All saved pages
│   ├── MapPage.svelte    Library map + list view
│   ├── Extension.svelte  Extension download and install steps
│   ├── Privacy.svelte
│   └── Callback.svelte   Sign-in redirect
├── components/
│   ├── Header, SearchBar (with voice), ResultRow, PageRow, LetterTile,
│   ├── AccountMenu, ConfirmDialog, Toasts, ScrollPill, EmptyState, ...
│   └── map/              MapCanvas (SVG), MapPanel, MapList, MapSkeleton
└── lib/                  router, highlight, time, domain, deletes, mapView

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Routing is a small history-based router in lib/router.js. Caddy serves index.html for every path.
  • Sign-in: the access token is kept in memory only. The refresh token is in localStorage, so a reload stays signed in. Because of that, the app never renders user-supplied HTML, and Caddy sends a strict Content Security Policy.
  • Map drawing is plain SVG in two layers, topics and pages. The geometry (fit, zoom, pan, culling, detail levels) is pure functions in lib/mapView.js, unit-tested with vitest.
  • Native scrollbars are hidden; a small floating pill shows the scroll position.
  • In development, Vite proxies /api to http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: Extension
docs.text:
The extension is Manifest V3, in code/src/extension, written as plain ES modules.

File Role background.js Service worker: sign-in, save, undo, auto-capture, excluded sites, Alt+Shift+M auth.js Cognito PKCE through chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow; tokens in chrome.storage.local api.js Authenticated fetch with one refresh-and-retry content.js Injected on demand; returns the page's HTML, text and canonical URL page_filter.js Auto-capture eligibility, saveable pages, excluded-site matching site_marker.js Runs only on memorylane.site; tells the site the extension is installed popup.*, options.* The popup and the excluded-sites page config.js Website, API and Cognito endpoints

The extension's ID is fixed by the public key in manifest.json (igdbkkmpnplmboeccgigbjgoefecdhck), so its Cognito redirect URL is the same on every machine.

docs.title: Library Map
docs.text: The library map (GET /map) turns a user's saved pages into named topics laid out on a 2-D canvas. It is built on request from the page vectors already in Solr, in backend/library_map.py, and cached per user.

docs.title: Page vectors
docs.text:
When a page is saved, its page vector (the normalised mean of its chunk vectors) is stored in page_embedding on chunk 0. The map and related pages both use it.

Related pages (GET /memory/{id}/related) is a KNN over page vectors, pre-filtered to the user's pages minus the page itself.

docs.title: Building the map
docs.text:
Newest MAP_MAX_PAGES (2,000) page vectors (cursor scan)
        ↓
PCA to ~50 dimensions, normalise
        ↓
k-means for each k in a range; keep the best silhouette
        ↓
Split any topic holding > 25% of pages (and > 30 pages)
        ↓
Unclustered: pages far from their centre, and loose "topics"
        ↓
Topic names
        ↓
Layout: ovals packed in rows, then relaxed
        ↓
Links: page → 2 nearest in topic; topic ↔ similar topic

docs.title: Choosing the number of topics
docs.text: For \(n\) pages, k-means is tried for every \(k\) from \(\mathrm{clamp}(\mathrm{round}(\sqrt{n}/2), 3, 10)\) to \(\min(14, n/8)\). The \(k\) with the best silhouette score (cosine, on a sample, fixed seed) wins. Topics holding more than a quarter of the library are split in two, repeatedly, so one broad topic can't swallow the map. On 278 SciFact abstracts this gives 9 topics.

docs.title: Outliers
docs.text: A page whose cosine similarity to its topic centre is below MAP_OUTLIER_SIMILARITY (0.35) is left unclustered. So is a whole "topic" whose pages don't hang together (mean pairwise similarity below 0.35²). Unclustered pages are drawn between the topics they are closest to.

docs.title: Topic names
docs.text:
1. Gemini, in one call for the whole map: for each topic it sees up to 10 page titles, a keyword hint, and the names already taken. It is asked for distinct, specific names of 1–3 words. Generic names ("Articles", "Resources", ...) and duplicates are rejected.
  2. Fallback: c-TF-IDF over the unigrams and bigrams of each topic's titles and descriptions, with generic words and title filler removed, made into distinct Title Case names.

Every fallback is logged at WARNING. Names are cached by topic membership, so an unchanged topic keeps its name and costs no Gemini call.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
All coordinates are in a 0–1 box, drawn into a 1400 × 900 world:

  • Each topic is an ellipse whose area is proportional to its page count. Together the ellipses cover about 30% of the canvas.
  • Topics are packed into centred rows matching the canvas's aspect ratio, ordered by a PCA of their centres so similar topics sit near each other. A few rounds of repulsion and centre pull then even out the gaps.
  • Each topic's label space is reserved, so a label never sits on another oval.
  • Pages are placed inside their ellipse by a local PCA, so similar pages sit together.

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
• Inside a topic: each page links to its 2 nearest neighbours. These are drawn only for the hovered or selected topic, and for the selected page.
  • Between topics: topics whose centres have cosine similarity above MAP_CROSS_TOPIC_SIMILARITY (0.65) get a dashed oval-to-oval link, at most 2 per topic, strongest first.

docs.title: Caching and freshness
docs.text: MapService keeps an LRU of up to 50 users' maps for 10 minutes. Saving or deleting a page invalidates that user's map, and each map has a version. GET /map/search and topic-filtered search use the cached map; if the version a client holds is gone, topic search returns 409.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Building a 2,000-page map takes about 0.2 s on a laptop, most of it k-means. The web app keeps the canvas readable and cheap to draw by dimming dots in libraries over 150 pages until you zoom past 1.6×, and by drawing only the links that matter for the current hover or selection.

docs.text:

│ save, auto-save  │   │ search, map, lib │  PKCE  │ Google / email   │
└────────┬─────────┘   └────────┬─────────┘        └──────────────────┘
         │  HTTPS + Bearer access token
         ▼                      ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Caddy: TLS, static web app, /api proxy  │
└────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
                     ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────┐
│ FastAPI backend                         │───────▶│ Gemini           │
│ token check → user_id                   │        │ (optional)       │
│ ingest · retrieval · map · summaries    │        └──────────────────┘
│ Sentence Transformers (bge-small)       │
└────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
                     ▼   always filtered by user_id

│ Apache Solr 9.7 · core memorylane_v2    │
│ BM25 (text_en) + HNSW vectors           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘

All three server pieces run with Docker Compose on one EC2 instance. Only Caddy is reachable from the internet.

docs.title: Chrome extension
docs.text: The collection layer. It saves the current page on request, runs optional auto-capture with its eligibility rules and excluded sites, and signs in with Cognito through chrome.identity. It doesn't search; searching happens on the website.

docs.title: Svelte web app
docs.text: The search interface: home with recent pages, results with snippets and summaries, the library, the library map, the extension page, privacy and the account menu. It is built into static files that Caddy serves.

docs.title: Amazon Cognito
docs.text: Hosts sign-in (Google, or email and password) and issues access tokens. The web app and extension both use the authorization-code flow with PKCE and a public client.

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text: Gets and renews HTTPS certificates, serves the web app with a strict Content Security Policy, serves the extension zip, proxies /api/* to the backend, and redirects www.memorylane.site to memorylane.site.

docs.title: FastAPI backend
docs.text: The application layer. It verifies every request's token, then saves pages, searches, builds library maps, finds related pages and asks Gemini for summaries, all scoped to the token's user. It loads the embedding model once at start-up.

docs.title: Apache Solr
docs.text: Stores chunks, page vectors and metadata, and runs BM25 and KNN search. It is bound to localhost on the server.

docs.title: Gemini
docs.text: Optional. Summarises a single page on request, and names library-map topics. Without a key, both fall back gracefully.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
• The server owns identity. User ids come only from verified tokens.
  • One ingest path. The API, scripts and evaluation all save pages through ingest_page, so they behave identically.
  • Search is page-level. Retrieval works on chunks, but users see pages.
  • Optional parts stay optional. Gemini and the reranker can be off without breaking search.

docs.title: Processing Architecture
docs.text: Every page enters MemoryLane through one function, ingest_page(user_id, url, title, content, html, canonical_url, is_manual) in backend/ingest.py. The API, scripts/reindex.py, scripts/backfill_page_vectors.py and the evaluation scripts all call it, so a page is processed the same way whichever path it came in by.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
Request (url, title, content, html?, canonical_url?, is_manual)
      ↓
Canonical URL preferred → normalise → page_id = sha256(user_id|url)[:32]
      ↓
YouTube? ── yes ─▶ transcript + metadata (built from the video id)
      │ no
      ▼
trafilatura on html (fallback: content) → tidy
      ↓
< 50 words? → 422
      ↓
Same content_hash and embedding_model as stored? → "unchanged"
      ↓
Chunk → embed "title + chunk" → page vector = normalised mean
      ↓
description = meta description or first readable sentences
      ↓
Upsert {page_id}::0..n-1 → delete chunks ≥ n
      ↓
Invalidate the user's library map

docs.title: Idempotence
docs.text:
• The content_hash is a SHA-256 of the cleaned text. Saving an unchanged page costs one Solr lookup.
  • If the stored embedding_model differs from the current one, the page is re-embedded even when the text is unchanged. Switching models therefore only needs a re-save or re-index, not a schema change.
  • Pages stored before description existed are re-ingested once, on their next save, to gain it. Pages without a page_embedding get one from scripts/backfill_page_vectors.py.

docs.title: Why the chunk upsert works this way
docs.text:
Solr has no transactions across documents. Writing the new chunks first, then deleting only those numbered past the new count, means a reader always sees a complete version of the page: the old one or the new one, never an empty page.

The backfill never uses Solr atomic updates. Those rewrite the document from its stored fields, and the chunk embedding field is not stored, so an atomic update would silently drop it.

docs.title: Retrieval Architecture
docs.text:
Search combines two complementary retrievers:

  1. Lexical (BM25) finds pages that use the query's words, including exact names, codes and jargon.
  2. Semantic (vector KNN) finds pages about the same idea, even in different words.

Both run over chunks and are restricted to the signed-in user's pages. Their rankings are fused, grouped into pages, filtered for relevance, and given snippets.

Query
  ├─▶ BM25 (edismax on title^2 text)          ─┐
  └─▶ embed query → KNN on chunk embeddings   ─┤  top 50 chunks each, user-filtered
                                               ▼
                         Reciprocal Rank Fusion
                                               ▼
                       (optional) cross-encoder rerank
                                               ▼
                        Group chunks by page_id
                                               ▼
                           Relevance floor
                                               ▼
                       Snippets → top-K pages

The BM25 query and the query embedding run concurrently.

docs.title: Lexical retrieval
docs.text: Solr's edismax parser searches title^2 text, with a phrase boost pf=text^2 title^3 so pages containing the query as a phrase rank higher. Both fields use text_en (possessives, stopwords, Porter stemming), so learning matches learn. Field queries in user input are disabled (uf=-*).

docs.title: Semantic retrieval
docs.text: The query is embedded with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (with BGE's search instruction in front) into the same 384-dimensional space as the chunks. Solr runs {!knn f=embedding topK=50} with the user filter as a pre-filter, so the 50 nearest chunks are all the user's own.

docs.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
docs.text:
BM25 scores and cosine similarities are on different scales, so MemoryLane fuses ranks, not scores. For a chunk \(d\):

\[ \mathrm{RRF}(d) = \frac{w_{\mathrm{bm25}}}{k + r_{\mathrm{bm25}}(d)} + \frac{w_{\mathrm{knn}}}{k + r_{\mathrm{knn}}(d)} \]

with \(k = 60\) and both weights 1.0. A chunk missing from one list gets nothing from it. Chunks found by both retrievers rise to the top.

Earlier versions

The first version min-max normalised the two score lists and averaged them (0.5 / 0.5). Min-max depends on the highest and lowest score in each list, so a single outlier changes every other score. RRF uses only ranks and has no such dependence.

docs.title: Optional reranking
docs.text: With RERANK_ENABLED=true, the top 20 fused chunks are re-scored by a cross-encoder (cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) that reads the query and chunk together. It is off on the live site to save memory.

docs.title: Page-level grouping
docs.text:
Users see pages, not chunks. Chunks are grouped by page_id, and each page scores:

\[ S_{\mathrm{page}} = s_{\mathrm{best}} + 0.3 \cdot s_{\mathrm{second}} \]

so a page with two good passages beats a page with one, without long pages winning just by having many chunks.

docs.title: Relevance floor
docs.text: KNN always returns 50 neighbours, however unrelated. A page with no BM25 match is dropped unless its best chunk's cosine similarity is at least MIN_VECTOR_SIMILARITY (0.55). Solr reports KNN scores as \((1 + \cos)/2\), so the backend converts them first. Pages that match a query word are always kept.

docs.title: Snippets
docs.text: For each result, backend/snippets.py picks 2–3 consecutive readable sentences around the sentence that contains the most query terms. Ties are broken by embedding similarity to the query. A readable sentence has 8+ words, is at least 70% letters, has no table pipes and ends in punctuation. Snippets are 200–280 characters. If no sentence qualifies, the page's stored description is used.

docs.title: Search within a topic
docs.text: POST /search with a topic restricts both retrievers to the page ids in that library-map topic. If the user's map has changed since the topic id was issued, the API returns 409, and the web app finds the topic again by name.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text: "debug": true adds each page's bm25_rank, knn_rank, fused_score, vector_similarity and per-stage timings to the response. The CLI prints the same with --debug.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: MemoryLane is multi-user, so the main security property is isolation: nobody can read, search, summarise, map or delete another person's pages.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• Sign-in is handled by Amazon Cognito (Google, or email and password). MemoryLane never handles passwords.
  • The web app and the extension use the authorization-code flow with PKCE and a public client (no client secret).
  • Every API request except GET /health needs Authorization: Bearer <access token>.

docs.title: Token verification
docs.text:
backend/auth.py verifies each access token:

  • RS256 signature against the user pool's JWKS (keys cached for an hour)
  • exp (not expired)
  • iss (this user pool)
  • token_use == "access" (ID tokens are refused)
  • client_id (this app client)

The user id is the token's sub. No endpoint accepts a user id from the client.

docs.title: Data isolation
docs.text:
• SolrClient adds {!term f=user_id}<sub> to every query, scan, KNN search and delete, and raises an error if the id is missing or malformed. Isolation doesn't depend on each endpoint remembering to filter.
  • KNN searches use the filter as a pre-filter, so other users' vectors are never candidates.
  • page_id includes the user id in its hash, so two users' copies of a page never collide.
  • A request for someone else's page gets 404, the same as a missing page, so page ids can't be probed.
  • tests/test_isolation.py checks this with two users: search, summaries, deletes, status, library, export, delete-all, the map, map search, related pages and topic search, plus a check that every Solr request carries the user filter.

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
• Only Caddy (ports 80 and 443) is public. HTTP redirects to HTTPS, with HSTS.
  • Solr is bound to 127.0.0.1. The backend has no published port and is reachable only through Caddy.

docs.title: Browser
docs.text:
• The access token lives in memory only. The refresh token is in localStorage, so a reload stays signed in.
  • Because a script on the page could read that refresh token, the app never renders user-supplied HTML (Svelte's {@html} is not used), and Caddy sends a strict Content Security Policy: scripts from the site only, connections only to the site and Cognito, no framing, no plugins.
  • The extension stores its tokens in chrome.storage.local, which web pages can't read.

docs.title: Abuse limits
docs.text:
• Rate limits per user (or per IP before sign-in), from 5/minute for export and delete-all to 120/minute for light reads.
  • Request size limits: URL 2,048 characters, title 500, text 500 KB, HTML 3 MB, query 500 characters.
  • The backend never fetches a URL supplied by the client. YouTube requests are built from a validated video id.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: .env (Cognito ids, Gemini key) and the extension's private signing key are kept out of git.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: MemoryLane runs on one machine with Docker Compose. The live site is an AWS EC2 c7i-flex.large (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, plus 2 GB swap) in the Mumbai region, with an Elastic IP and the domain memorylane.site.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Service What it does Reachable from solr Solr 9.7 with a 1 GB heap; data in a named volume 127.0.0.1:8983 on the server only backend FastAPI and the embedding model (cached in the models volume) Caddy only; no published port caddy Gets HTTPS certificates, serves the built web app and the extension zip, proxies /api/* to the backend, redirects www. Ports 80 and 443 
Browser / extension ──HTTPS──▶ Caddy ──/api──▶ FastAPI ──▶ Solr
                                 │
                                 └── web app (static) + /memorylane-extension.zip

The Caddy image builds the web app (npm run build) and zips the extension/ folder, so https://memorylane.site/memorylane-extension.zip always matches the code being deployed.

docs.title: First deployment
docs.text:
From code/src on the server:

cp .env.example .env              # fill in Cognito, Gemini, DOMAIN
docker compose up -d solr
docker compose exec solr solr create -c memorylane_v2 -d _default
CORE_NAME=memorylane_v2 bash scripts/setup_solr.sh
docker compose up -d --build
curl -s https://<your-domain>/api/health

Before that, point the domain's A records (with and without www.) at the server and open ports 80 and 443. Ports 8000 and 8983 should stay closed.

The repository's code/src/deploy/README.md is the full step-by-step guide. It covers swap, moving data from an older core, the reboot test, and backups with EBS snapshots.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
cd code/src
git pull origin master
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose logs -f backend

Rebuilding the backend clears its in-memory map and label caches. Maps are rebuilt on the next request.

docs.title: Schema changes
docs.text:
Solr's automatic field creation is turned off, so a new field has to exist before the backend that writes it is deployed:

Field Added by Then description scripts/add_description_field.sh Pages get one the next time they're saved page_embedding scripts/add_page_embedding_field.sh python -m scripts.backfill_page_vectors gives older pages a page vector (resumable)

Warning

Never run docker compose down -v. It deletes Solr's data, the downloaded models and Caddy's certificates.

docs.title: Moving pages between cores
docs.text:
scripts/reindex.py copies pages from one core into another under a given user id, re-cleaning, re-chunking and re-embedding them. The source core is never modified.

docker compose exec backend python -m scripts.reindex \
  --source-core memorylane --target-core memorylane_v2 --user-id <cognito-sub> [--dry-run]

docs.title: Retrieval quality
docs.text: Retrieval quality is measured separately, with the SciFact evaluation, because it needs a real Solr core and the embedding model.

docs.title: Manual check
docs.text:
1. GET /health → all true
  2. Save a page from the extension → it appears under Recently saved
  3. Save it again → unchanged, same chunk count
  4. Search with different wording from the page → it's found, with a sensible snippet
  5. Summarise → a summary (with a Gemini key)
  6. Open Map with 10+ pages → named topics; click a page → related pages
  7. Sign in as a second user → none of the first user's pages are visible

docs.title: Evaluation Methodology
docs.text: MemoryLane's retrieval is evaluated on SciFact, a scientific-claim retrieval dataset from the BEIR benchmark, adapted to MemoryLane's data model.

docs.title: Corpus and queries
docs.text:
• 1,000 SciFact abstracts as documents
  • 100 claims as queries
  • 106 relevant documents across 115 query–document pairs (binary relevance)

Each document gets a synthetic URL of the form:

https://scifact.org/doc/{document_id}

The URLs only give each document a unique identity; titles and text come from SciFact. This is a controlled retrieval benchmark, not a live-web crawl.

docs.title: How it runs
docs.text:
The evaluation uses the same code as production:

  • Documents are saved through ingest_page, the same function behind POST /memory, so cleaning, chunking, embedding and indexing are all exercised.
  • Queries go through hybrid_search, the same function behind POST /search.
  • Everything runs under the user id eval, in a separate core (memorylane_eval by default), so benchmark data never mixes with real users.
cd code/src
CORE_NAME=memorylane_eval ./scripts/setup_solr.sh
python -m evaluation.scifact_ingest      # index the 1,000 documents
python -m evaluation.scifact_evaluate    # writes evaluation/scifact_report.json

docs.title: Configurations compared
docs.text: Configuration What it uses BM25 only Lexical retrieval Vector only Dense retrieval Hybrid The production pipeline: both, fused

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
• MRR@10: how early the first relevant result appears
  • Recall@10: how much of the relevant set is in the top ten
  • nDCG@10: how well the relevant results are ordered

Relevant URLs are compared after normalisation.

docs.title: Second evaluation: generated queries
docs.text: evaluation/generate_eval.py builds queries from pages already indexed, and evaluation/evaluate.py reports Recall@1/3/5/10 and MRR for them. This is a quick check on your own data rather than a benchmark.

docs.title: Evaluation Results
docs.text:
Which version these numbers come from

These results were measured on the earlier retrieval pipeline: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, 300–500-word chunks, and min-max score fusion (0.5 / 0.5). The current pipeline (bge-small-en-v1.5, 150-word overlapping chunks with titles, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, a relevance floor) has not been re-benchmarked yet. Run the commands in Methodology to measure it.

Method MRR@10 Recall@10 nDCG@10 BM25 only 0.6482 0.8117 0.6776 Vector only 0.7795 0.8867 0.8008 Hybrid (min-max fusion) 0.7538 0.9167 0.7890

docs.title: BM25
docs.text: A solid lexical baseline. It works well when the query uses the same terms as the document.

docs.title: Vector retrieval
docs.text: Vector retrieval had the best MRR@10 and nDCG@10: it put a relevant abstract at the top most often.

docs.title: Hybrid retrieval
docs.text:
Hybrid retrieval had the best Recall@10: it found the largest share of relevant abstracts in the top ten. Its MRR@10 and nDCG@10 were slightly below vector-only, so mixing in BM25 scores sometimes moved the first relevant result down a place.

No single method won every metric, which motivated the later changes:

  • Reciprocal Rank Fusion, which combines ranks instead of raw scores
  • A stronger embedding model (BGE) with a search instruction for queries
  • Smaller, overlapping chunks embedded with the page title
  • A relevance floor, so weak vector-only matches are dropped instead of shown

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: There are two ways to use MemoryLane.

docs.title: Use the hosted site
docs.text:
1. Open memorylane.site and sign in with Google or with email.
  2. Install the Chrome extension from memorylane.site/extension and sign in from its popup.
  3. On any page worth keeping, open the extension and press Remember this page.
  4. Back on the website, describe what you're looking for.

Each account has its own private library. See Running MemoryLane for details.

docs.title: Run your own copy
docs.text:
MemoryLane is open source. To run it on your machine or your own server:

  1. Installation: Python, Solr 9 and the web app.
  2. Configuration: the .env file and a Cognito user pool.
  3. Running MemoryLane: start the API, the web app and the extension locally.
  4. Deployment: Docker Compose and Caddy on a server.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Settings come from code/src/.env. Start from .env.example. The .env file holds secrets and is ignored by git.

docs.title: Sign-in (Amazon Cognito)
docs.text:
The API refuses to start without a Cognito pool. Create one with:

  • An app client with no client secret (a public client using PKCE), the Authorization code grant, and the scopes openid, email and profile.
  • Allowed callback URLs: https://<your-domain>/auth/callback, http://localhost:5173/auth/callback, and the extension's https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/.
  • Allowed sign-out URLs: https://<your-domain>/ and http://localhost:5173/.
  • Identity providers: the Cognito user pool, and optionally Google.
Variable Purpose COGNITO_REGION, COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID, COGNITO_APP_CLIENT_ID The pool whose access tokens the API accepts VITE_COGNITO_DOMAIN Hosted sign-in domain, e.g. https://<prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID Same app client id, used by the web app VITE_REDIRECT_URI, VITE_LOGOUT_URI Where Cognito returns after sign-in and sign-out VITE_API_BASE Where the web app sends API calls (/api behind Caddy; the dev server proxies it) CORS_ORIGINS Comma-separated origins allowed to call the API (default http://localhost:5173)

docs.title: Solr and embeddings
docs.text:
Variable Default Purpose SOLR_URL http://localhost:8983/solr/memorylane_v2 Core URL EMBEDDING_MODEL BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 Sentence Transformers model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 also works) EMBEDDING_DIM 384 Must match the Solr vector field EMBEDDING_QUERY_PREFIX BGE search instruction Added to queries only; leave empty for MiniLM

Changing the model means re-embedding every page.

docs.text: Variable Default Purpose CHUNK_MAX_WORDS 150 Largest chunk CHUNK_MIN_WORDS 40 A last chunk with fewer new words merges into the previous one CHUNK_OVERLAP_WORDS 30 Words carried over from the previous chunk

docs.title: Extension
docs.text: extension/config.js holds the website URL, API URL and Cognito settings the extension uses. The extension's ID is pinned by the key in manifest.json, so its sign-in redirect URL stays the same on every install.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: All application code is in code/src of the repository. Commands below run from that folder.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10+
  • Apache Solr 9.x (9.7 is the tested version). Solr 8 has no DenseVectorField, so it won't work.
  • Node.js 18+ for the web app
  • Docker (recommended, for Solr, or for the whole stack)
  • Chrome or Chromium for the extension
  • An Amazon Cognito user pool (see Configuration)
  • Optional: a Google Gemini API key for summaries and map topic names

docs.title: 1. Backend
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/rabeeh18/ucs503p-202627-MemoryLane.git
cd ucs503p-202627-MemoryLane/code/src
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env               # Windows: copy .env.example .env

The first start downloads the embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, about 130 MB) from Hugging Face.

docs.title: 2. Solr
docs.text:
Start Solr 9.7, for example with the project's Compose file:

docker compose up -d solr
docker compose exec solr solr create -c memorylane_v2 -d _default

Then install the schema. The script is idempotent: it checks the Solr version, creates the core if needed, applies the fields, turns off automatic field creation, and finishes with a smoke test (indexing, BM25 with stemming, KNN with a user filter).

CORE_NAME=memorylane_v2 ./scripts/setup_solr.sh      # Linux / macOS
.\scripts\setup_solr.ps1                              # Windows PowerShell

Add --reset (or -Reset) to drop and recreate the core. This deletes its data.

docs.title: 3. Web app
docs.text:
cd frontend
npm install

The web app reads its VITE_* settings from the same .env file in code/src.

docs.title: 4. Extension
docs.text:
chrome://extensions → turn on Developer mode → Load unpacked → choose code/src/extension.

The extension talks to the hosted site by default. To point it at a local backend, change the endpoints in extension/config.js. See Configuration.

docs.title: The hosted site
docs.text:
MemoryLane runs at memorylane.site.

  1. Sign in with Continue with Google or with email. Each account has its own private, empty library.
  2. Get the extension from memorylane.site/extension:
    1. Download memorylane-extension.zip and unzip it.
    2. Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode.
    3. Click Load unpacked and choose the unzipped folder.
    4. Pin MemoryLane to the toolbar, open it, and sign in.
  3. Save pages with Remember this page in the extension popup. You can also turn on automatic capture there.
  4. Search on the website by describing what you remember. Your library, the map and related pages fill up as you save more.

Once the extension is installed, the website stops showing "Get the extension".

docs.title: Running it locally
docs.text:
After installation and configuration, with Solr running:

# API (from code/src)
uvicorn backend.main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
curl http://localhost:8000/health
# {"status":"ok","solr":true,"embedding_model":true,"gemini":true}

# Web app (from code/src/frontend)
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173, proxies /api to http://127.0.0.1:8000

/health reports status: ok when Solr and the embedding model are ready. Gemini is optional, so gemini: false is fine.

docs.title: Command-line search
docs.text:
Search a user's pages without the web app:

python -m backend.cli "your query" --user-id <cognito-sub> --top-k 5 --debug --no-summarize

--debug prints each page's BM25 rank, KNN rank, fused score and timings.

docs.title: Running it on a server
docs.text: The production setup is Docker Compose with Solr, the backend and Caddy on one machine. See Deployment.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
This section follows a page from the moment you save it to the moment you find it again.

  • System Overview
  • Capturing Web Content
  • Content Processing
  • Storage

docs.title: Capturing Web Content
docs.text: The Chrome extension is MemoryLane's collection layer. The server does the cleaning.

docs.title: What the extension sends
docs.text:
When you save a page (or auto-capture picks one up), the extension injects content.js into the tab, which returns:

  • The page's full HTML
  • Its visible text (the fallback if cleaning finds nothing)
  • The canonical URL, if the page declares one

The service worker posts these, with the URL, title and whether the save was manual, to POST /api/memory, using the signed-in user's access token. If the token has expired, the extension refreshes it once and retries.

Auto-capture also checks the page against the capture rules and your excluded sites before sending anything, and doesn't send a URL again while a save of it is in progress, or within a minute of auto-capturing it.

docs.title: What the backend does
docs.text:
All of this happens in one function, ingest_page (backend/ingest.py). It is shared by the API, the re-index and backfill scripts and the evaluation.

  1. Take the user id from the verified token (never from the request).
  2. Prefer the canonical URL, then normalise it.
  3. Compute page_id = sha256(user_id | normalised URL)[:32].
  4. YouTube: fetch the transcript and metadata instead of using the page (see YouTube Videos).
  5. Other pages: extract the main text from the HTML with trafilatura. If that fails, use the extension's text.
  6. Reject the page with 422 if it has fewer than 50 words.
  7. If the page is already stored with the same content hash and embedding model, return unchanged and do nothing.
  8. Chunk, embed, compute the page vector and description.
  9. Upsert the chunks as {page_id}::{n}, then delete any higher-numbered chunks left from an older, longer version.
  10. Clear the user's cached library map.

The response is {status: saved | unchanged | skipped, message, page}.

docs.title: Duplicates
docs.text: Because page_id is derived from the normalised URL, the same page saved twice (with or without www., tracking parameters or a fragment) updates one entry instead of creating two. Different users saving the same URL get separate entries.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text: MemoryLane is two pipelines that meet in Solr: one that saves pages and one that finds them. Both run under the signed-in user's id.

docs.title: Saving a page
docs.text:
Page in Chrome (or a YouTube video)
          ↓
Extension: HTML + text + canonical URL
          ↓
Caddy (HTTPS) → FastAPI, with a Cognito access token
          ↓
Verify the token → user_id
          ↓
Normalise the URL → page_id = hash(user_id, URL)
          ↓
Clean (trafilatura) or fetch the transcript
          ↓
At least 50 words? Changed since last save?
          ↓
Chunk (≤150 words, 30-word overlap)
          ↓
Embed "title + chunk" (bge-small-en-v1.5, 384-d)
          ↓
Solr: chunks + page vector + description

docs.title: Finding it
docs.text:
Query (typed or spoken)
          ↓
Web app → Caddy → FastAPI (token → user_id)
          ↓
   ┌──────────────┬──────────────┐
BM25 (edismax)        Vector KNN (query embedding)
   └──────────────┴──────────────┘
          ↓   both filtered by user_id
Reciprocal Rank Fusion
          ↓
(optional cross-encoder rerank)
          ↓
Group chunks into pages
          ↓
Relevance floor
          ↓
Snippets → results

docs.title: Mapping the library
docs.text:
User's page vectors (newest 2,000)
          ↓
PCA → k-means (k chosen by silhouette) → split oversized topics
          ↓
Outliers left unclustered
          ↓
Topic names (Gemini, or keywords)
          ↓
Layout + links → cached per user

docs.title: Separation of responsibilities
docs.text: Part Responsibility Extension Collecting pages, auto-capture rules, excluded sites Web app Search, library, map, summaries, account Cognito Who the user is Caddy HTTPS, static files, routing /api FastAPI Token checks, ingest, retrieval, map, summaries Sentence Transformers Embeddings Solr Storage, BM25 and KNN search Gemini Optional summaries and topic names

docs.title: Content Processing
docs.text: Before it is stored, a saved page is cleaned and split into small passages, and each passage is turned into a vector.

docs.title: URL normalisation
docs.text:
The same page can have many URLs. MemoryLane normalises them by:

  • Lower-casing the scheme and host
  • Removing www.
  • Removing fragments (#...)
  • Removing trailing slashes (except the root /)
  • Removing tracking parameters: utm_*, fbclid, gclid, ref, ref_src
  • Sorting the remaining query parameters

The page id is the first 32 hex characters of sha256("{user_id}|{normalised_url}").

docs.title: Cleaning
docs.text:
Raw page text is full of menus, cookie banners, "related articles" lists and footers. MemoryLane runs trafilatura on the page's HTML to keep only the main content. If trafilatura finds fewer than 50 words, the text the extension sent is used instead. Either way, citation markers such as [4] and junk lines (dividers, table rules, icon rows, lone words) are removed and whitespace is tidied. YouTube transcripts skip trafilatura.

Pages with fewer than 50 words after cleaning are rejected.

docs.title: Chunking
docs.text:
The text is split into paragraphs, then sentences, and packed into chunks:

Rule Value Largest chunk 150 words Overlap each chunk starts with ~30 words of the previous chunk's last sentences Short tail a last chunk with under 40 new words merges into the one before Long sentences hard-split by words

Small, overlapping chunks keep each vector focused on one idea, and the overlap stops an idea being cut in half at a chunk boundary.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
Each chunk is embedded as title + chunk with:

BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5   (384 dimensions, L2-normalised)

Queries are embedded with BGE's search instruction (Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages:) in front. Passages are embedded without it. all-MiniLM-L6-v2 can be used instead by changing EMBEDDING_MODEL and clearing the prefix.

Embeddings are computed in batches of 32, and the last 1,024 query embeddings are cached.

docs.title: Page vector and description
docs.text:
Two more values are computed per page:

  • Page vector: the normalised mean of the page's chunk vectors. It powers related pages and the library map.
  • Description: the page's meta description, otherwise its first readable sentences (up to 300 characters). Snippets fall back to it when no sentence matches the query well.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: MemoryLane stores everything in Apache Solr 9.7, in a standalone core named memorylane_v2.

docs.title: Why Solr?
docs.text:
One system covers what MemoryLane needs:

  • Full-text search with BM25, English stemming and stopwords (text_en)
  • Dense-vector KNN search (DenseVectorField, HNSW, cosine) with pre-filtering, so a vector search only ever looks at one user's pages
  • Updates and deletes by query, and cursor-based scans

docs.title: Document model
docs.text:
Each chunk is one Solr document. Chunk 0 also carries the page-level fields.

Field Type Purpose id string {page_id}::{chunk_index} user_id string Owner (Cognito sub); every query filters on it page_id string Groups a page's chunks url string Normalised URL domain string Site title text_en Page title (boosted ×2 in search) text text_en Chunk text chunk_id, total_chunks int Position and count timestamp date When the page was saved content_hash string Skips re-processing unchanged pages embedding_model string Re-embeds when the model changes description string, stored only Snippet fallback embedding vector, 384-d, not stored Chunk vector for KNN page_embedding vector, 384-d, stored (chunk 0) Page vector for related pages and the map

scripts/setup_solr.sh is the single source of truth for this schema. Automatic field creation is turned off, so a document with an unknown field is rejected instead of silently adding a guessed field.

docs.title: Writes
docs.text:
• Saves use commitWithin (1 s) rather than explicit commits.
  • A re-saved page is upserted chunk by chunk, then any leftover higher-numbered chunks are deleted, so there are never duplicates.
  • Deleting a page deletes by user_id and page_id; deleting an account's data deletes by user_id.

docs.title: Isolation
docs.text: Every read, search, delete and scan in backend/solr_client.py adds a user_id filter, and refuses to run if the user id is missing or malformed. Vector searches pass the filter as a KNN pre-filter, so other users' vectors are never considered.

docs.title: Saving Pages
docs.text: Pages get into MemoryLane through the Chrome extension, in one of two ways.

docs.title: Remember this page
docs.text:
Open the extension on any page and press Remember this page.

  • The popup confirms Saved just now, with an Undo button.
  • If the page is already in your library, the popup says so and offers Remove.
  • Saving the same page again updates it. If its text hasn't changed, nothing is re-processed.
  • A page needs at least 50 readable words. Pages with less (an empty app screen, a login form) are refused with a message.

Alt+Shift+M opens the MemoryLane website from anywhere in Chrome.

docs.title: Automatic capture
docs.text:
Automatic capture saves eligible pages when they finish loading. It is off by default: you turn it on in the extension popup, and the first time you do, the popup explains what it does before enabling it.

It only runs while you're signed in. Signing out stops it.

Page finishes loading
        ↓
Auto-capture on, and signed in?
        ↓
Eligible page? Not an excluded site? Not MemoryLane itself?
        ↓
Extract the page (HTML + text)
        ↓
POST /api/memory
        ↓
Cleaned, chunked, embedded and stored under your account

docs.title: What automatic capture skips
docs.text:
• Social-media sites
  • Banks and payment services
  • Login, sign-up, account, password, checkout, billing, payment and wallet pages
  • Browser-internal pages (chrome://, chrome-extension://, file://, ...)
  • Search-engine result pages
  • Utility pages such as error, privacy, terms, cookie and sitemap pages
  • Files: PDF, images, audio and video, archives, CSV, JSON, XML
  • Pages with very little text
  • YouTube pages that aren't a video, and videos longer than two hours

docs.title: Excluded sites
docs.text:
From the popup you can exclude the current site with one click. The extension's options page lists every excluded site, and you can add or remove them there. Excluded sites are never captured automatically, but you can still save a page from them by hand.

Manual saving skips the automatic-capture filters: if you press Remember this page, the page is saved (as long as it has enough text).

docs.title: Recently saved
docs.text: The home page lists your most recently saved pages under the search box. View all opens the full library.

docs.title: All saved pages
docs.text: The library (/library) lists every page you saved, newest first, 20 at a time with Load more. Each row shows the title, site, letter tile and when you saved it.

docs.title: Deleting a page
docs.text:
Use the bin icon on a row in the library, home page or search results (or Shift + Del on a selected search result).

  • The page disappears at once and a toast offers Undo for 6 seconds.
  • After that, it's deleted from the server.
  • If you close the tab during those 6 seconds, the delete is sent straight away.
  • If the server can't delete it, the page comes back with an error message.

docs.title: Account menu
docs.text:
The circle at the top right shows your initial and opens the account menu:

Item What it does All saved pages Opens the library Get the extension Opens the extension page (hidden once the extension is installed) Export my data Downloads every saved page as JSON Delete all my data Deletes every page you saved, after a confirmation Sign out Signs out of the website

Signing out of the website doesn't sign out the extension. Sign out of it from its own popup.

docs.title: Library Map
docs.text:
Map in the header opens a picture of everything you've saved. Pages are dots, grouped into topics drawn as labelled ovals. A bigger oval means more pages.

The map needs at least 10 saved pages. With fewer, it asks you to save a few more.

docs.title: Moving around
docs.text:
• Scroll to zoom, drag to pan.
  • Fit (bottom left) brings the whole map back into view.
  • Find a topic… searches topic names and the pages inside them, and zooms to the best topic.
  • List shows the same topics and pages as a list.

In large libraries, page dots stay dim until you zoom in, so the topics stay readable.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
Click a topic to open its panel:

  • The topic's pages
  • Search only these pages, which runs a search inside that topic

Hovering over or selecting a topic shows the links between its pages. Dashed lines between ovals join topics that are about similar things.

Pages that don't fit any topic well sit between the ovals, smaller and dimmer, and show as Not in a topic.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
Click a dot to open its panel:

  • Title, site and when you saved it
  • Open page
  • Summarise
  • Related pages: your other saved pages closest in meaning to this one

The selected page's links to its nearest pages are highlighted.

On a phone the panel opens as a sheet from the bottom of the screen.

docs.title: When the map changes
docs.text:
Saving or deleting a page rebuilds the map the next time you open it. Topic names are kept when a topic's pages stay the same.

See Library Map Architecture for how topics and their names are made.

docs.title: Searching
docs.text:
Describe what you remember in the search box on the home page. Press / anywhere on the home page to jump to it.

the article on reducing database query latency

docs about ROS navigation

The query doesn't need the page's exact words. MemoryLane matches by meaning as well as by keywords.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Each result shows:

  • The page title, linking to the page
  • The site, with a letter tile for the domain
  • A snippet: two or three sentences from the page that best match your query, with the query words highlighted
  • When you saved it
  • Summarise, for a short summary of that page

Up to 10 pages are shown. Pages that only loosely match your query are left out instead of padding the list, so a short list means nothing else was close enough. If nothing matches, MemoryLane suggests describing the idea rather than exact words.

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text: Key Action ↑ ↓ Move between results Enter Open the selected page Shift + Del Delete the selected page (with undo) Esc Clear the search

docs.title: Searching within a topic
docs.text: From the library map, Search only these pages limits a search to one topic. The results page shows the topic as a chip; remove it to search everything again. If the topic changed because you saved or deleted pages in the meantime, MemoryLane finds the same topic by name, or searches all pages and tells you.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: Every search runs a keyword search (BM25) and a meaning search (vector KNN) over your pages at the same time, then combines them. See Retrieval Architecture.

docs.title: Summaries
docs.text:
Each search result, and each page selected on the map, has a Summarise button. It asks Google Gemini for a short summary of that one page.

Summarise
   ↓
POST /api/summarize {query, id}
   ↓
Load the page's stored text (your pages only)
   ↓
Gemini
   ↓
Summary shown under the result

docs.title: What Gemini sees
docs.text: Only the stored text of the page you chose (long pages are truncated), and your query. Gemini is asked to summarise that text only, without adding outside knowledge.

docs.title: Length
docs.text:
The wording of your query sets the length:

  • Short (1–2 sentences): words like brief, quick summary, tl;dr, in a nutshell
  • Long (2–3 short paragraphs): words like detailed, in-depth, comprehensive, explain fully
  • Medium otherwise

docs.title: When it's unavailable
docs.text: Summaries need a Gemini key on the server. Without one, or if Gemini fails, the result shows a short message instead, and search keeps working. GET /health reports whether Gemini is available.

docs.title: Voice Search
docs.text:
In browsers with speech recognition (Chrome and Edge), the search box shows a microphone button.

  1. Press the microphone and allow microphone access if the browser asks.
  2. Say your query.
  3. The recognised text appears in the search box.
  4. Press Enter to search.

Voice input only fills in the search box: the query then goes through the same search as a typed one. Speech recognition is done by the browser, not by MemoryLane.

If the browser has no speech recognition, the microphone button isn't shown.

docs.title: YouTube Videos
docs.text:
A YouTube video page has almost no readable text, so MemoryLane saves the video through its transcript instead.

youtube.com/watch?v=… or youtu.be/…
        ↓
Recognise the video id
        ↓
Fetch title, channel and duration
        ↓
Fetch the transcript
        ↓
Title + channel + duration + transcript
        ↓
Same pipeline as any page: chunk → embed → store

The backend builds the video's URL itself from the video id. It never fetches a URL sent by the browser.

docs.title: What gets stored
docs.text:
• Video title
  • Channel
  • Duration
  • The transcript text

You then find the video by what was said in it.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The video needs an available transcript (uploaded or auto-generated). Without one it can't be saved.
  • Automatic capture skips videos longer than two hours, and skips them when their length can't be determined. Remember this page saves them anyway.
  • YouTube pages that aren't a video (home, channels, search) are never captured automatically.
